reason: This text fragment (Exodus 1:15-22) depicts the Hebrews as a distinct people and growing nation within Egypt, but makes no reference to them possessing their own specific land. The passage centers on Hebrew people living under Egyptian rule, with Pharaoh issuing commands that govern the Hebrews in Egypt. The text portrays the Hebrews as a numerically growing nation (וַיִּרֶב הָעָם וַיַּֽעַצְמ֖וּ - 'the people multiplied and grew very mighty'), but provides no indication of territorial possession or a homeland distinct from Egypt. The absence of any mention of Hebrew-owned land, combined with the explicit context of Egyptian sovereignty over the Hebrew population, indicates that this passage does not support the stated claim.
